intro: A bicycle chained to a post. Tires flat, chain good.

text: Chain, gears, cables. All of it useful.
The bolts are fused. Got a sore wrist, nothing else.

options.label: Pump the tires and ride it a while

text: Flew down three blocks. Felt like being twelve.
Front tire burst. Walked it back to where I started.

intro: Crows. Hundreds, on every wire, all watching me.

text: They lost interest. One followed me for a block, though.
They all took off at once. The noise. Anything nearby heard it.
Not one moved. I don't like that either.
They dove. Pecked my neck and scalp. Just scratches.

intro: A shopping cart on its side, full of pill bottles. Labels faded.

options.label: Sort them, read what you can

text: Antibiotics and painkillers. The real thing.
Can't read half of them. Took nothing: not worth the risk.
Something in here will be useful. Probably.
Vitamins. All vitamins. Great.

intro: Clean laundry on a line between two balconies. Someone hung it recently.

options.label: Call out to whoever lives here

text: An old man waves from the window. Trades me a jar of beans for news.
A door slams. Then silence. Then a dog, inside, very big.

options.label: Leave it alone and move on

text: Somebody's still living here. That's... good. I think.
Felt eyes on my back for two blocks.

intro: A school bus, doors open, backpacks still on the seats.

text: Snacks, a flashlight, batteries. And a drawing I folded into my pocket.
Just notebooks. I couldn't stop reading the names.
The battery's dead but the alternator's fine. Coming with me.
Engine's been stripped already.
Some places you just don't go in.
I went in anyway in my head. All day.

intro: A dog, skinny, wagging. It wants to follow me.

text: It ate and walked beside me a while. Then it barked at a doorway: someone had stashed cans there.
success.memory: the dog that walked with me

text: It ate and ran off. Fair.
It left. Looked back twice.
It kept following and barking. Had to hide.

intro: The footbridge is down. The river underneath is low, but fast.

text: Soaked to the waist, but across.
The current took my feet. Banged my knee on a rock.

options.label: Walk upstream to the next bridge

text: Long way. Found a dry crossing.
The next bridge was down too. Back to the start.

options.label: Rig a line from the wreckage

text: Took a while, but the line held. I'll leave it for next time.
The line slipped. Gave up and walked around.

intro: An old army checkpoint. Sandbags, a barrier, nobody. A rifle rack, empty.

text: Radio batteries and a logbook. Last entry: 'they're not coming back for us'.
Rats. Nothing but rats.
Nothing. Kept going.
Tripped a can-alarm. Hid for twenty minutes.

intro: The stairwell is pitch black. Something drips, far above.

text: Just water. A whole floor of storage at the top.
The light caught something on the landing. It moved. I didn't stay.

options.label: Climb in the dark, by touch

text: Quiet all the way up. Found a stash by feel.
Missed a step. Twisted my ankle.

intro: A lone trader with a handcart. Wants batteries, offers food.

text: A fair deal. She even threw in a tip about the road ahead.
She short-changed me and I noticed too late.
Got the better end. She laughed about it. I liked her.
She packed up and left. No deal.
Nodded and moved on.
She followed a while, asking. Annoying.

intro: A rooftop greenhouse. Most of it dead. Some tomatoes, gone wild.

text: Small, sour, real tomatoes. I almost cried.
All rotten under the leaves.
Seeds in a twist of paper. Someone at home will know what to do.
success.memory: seeds from the rooftop greenhouse

text: Dropped them through a crack in the floor.

intro: I bumped a car and its alarm went off. After all these years.

options.label: Pop the hood and kill it

text: Silenced. And look: a battery that still works.
Couldn't find the wire. It screamed for a full minute.
Two blocks away, under a truck. Nothing came.
Something came. I didn't see it. I heard it sniffing.

intro: A supermarket. The front's been looted to the floor. The loading bay hasn't.

text: Crates. Real ones. Flour gone hard, but cans.
Pulled something in my back.
Things roll under shelves. Three cans and a lighter.
Glass and mouse droppings.

intro: A body against a wall, long gone. A note pinned to the jacket.

text: 'Tell Ana I tried.' And a key taped underneath. It opened a locker nearby.
success.memory: the note that said 'tell Ana I tried'

text: I couldn't. I just couldn't.
Put my coat over the face. It felt right.
Couldn't look away for a long time.

intro: Hail. Sudden, hard, the size of marbles.

text: Waited it out in a bus stop. Ice everywhere after.
The roof I picked leaked. Soaked and cold.
Ugly, but I made good time.
Got hit in the head. Seeing stars.

intro: A gas station. The lights are on. Somebody's got a generator here.

text: A woman with a shotgun and a kind face. Gave me water and a tip.
A shot over my head. I left fast.
Her spare fuel cans. I took one. I'm not proud.
A dog. A big dog. I ran.
Not my business.
Longer way around than I thought.

intro: A cell tower, with a maintenance cabinet at the base.

text: Circuit boards, good copper, a backup battery.
Shocked myself. Some cell's still charged.

options.label: Climb a few meters to look around

text: Saw the whole district from up there. Easier route back.
Froze halfway. Came down slow.

intro: Chalk on the sidewalk: a hopscotch, and an arrow, fresh. 'FOOD →'

text: A little cache in a mailbox. Someone's leaving it for strangers.
The arrow led to an empty lot. Then I found another arrow pointing back at me.
Arrows lead places. I'm not going to that place.
I'll wonder about it all night.

intro: The mall's escalator is stopped, and something's moving at the top of it.

text: A family of foxes. They left. I took the stairs.
Whatever it was came down. I left through the cinema.
Foxes. They scattered. The electronics shop up there was untouched.
It wasn't foxes. I ran. It didn't follow. Yet.

intro: Far off, a train horn. There are no trains.

text: An old horn on a timer, on a pole. Wired to a car battery. Mine now.
Walked toward it for an hour. It kept being far away.
Whatever it is, it can blow its horn without me.
It blew again. Closer.

intro: The underpass is flooded knee-deep. The road beyond is the fast way.

text: Cold and disgusting. Fast.
Something brushed my leg. I sprinted the rest.

options.label: Go over the top, along the railings

text: Balanced the whole way. Dry feet.
Slipped and went in anyway.
Long. Boring. Dry.
Long, boring and it rained.

intro: A farmhouse with smoke from the chimney. Chickens in the yard.

text: Eggs! Real eggs. They asked about the radio. I told them how to find you.
Nobody answered. The chickens stared at me.
Got one. I'm a terrible person. A fed terrible person.
Farmer with a pitchfork. I'm faster. Barely.

intro: A small wind turbine on a farm, still spinning.

text: Charge controller, intact. The workshop will love this.
Wrong panel. Spent an hour on nothing.

options.label: Hook up the batteries you carry and wait

text: Charged everything I had. Slow, but free.
The wiring's fried. Waited for nothing.

intro: A pileup across all lanes of the highway. Dozens of cars.

text: Spare parts, a first aid kit, canned food. Somebody was ready.
Already picked clean. Long ago.
Car roofs all the way across. Quick.
Fell between two cars.

intro: At dusk, lights on a hill. Lots of them. Like a town.

text: Candles in jars, on graves. Hundreds. Someone tends them.
success.memory: the hill of candles

text: Someone was waiting by the lights. He saw me.

options.label: Mark it on the map and move on

text: Marked. The radio will want to know about this.
Lost the bearing in the dark.

intro: The road is too quiet. No birds. No wind.

text: There. A voice, far off. Someone singing. Then the birds came back.
Something, far behind me, stopped walking when I stopped.
Got through. Didn't look back.
Ran out of breath halfway. The quiet waited.

intro: A rooftop pigeon coop. A few birds still live there.

text: Four eggs, wrapped in my scarf. Careful now.
Broke them all climbing down.

options.label: There's a band on one bird's leg

text: A message: coordinates and 'supplies, take what you need'.
success.memory: the message on the pigeon's leg

text: Couldn't catch it.

intro: A hospital bed in the middle of the street. Clean sheets. Nobody around.

text: A medkit, tucked in neatly. Like a gift.
Under the sheets: nothing. On the pillow: my name.
Walked around it. Wide.
When I looked back, the sheets were folded down.

intro: A storm drain grate, pried open. Rungs go down into the dark.

text: Someone's old hideout. Blankets, cans, a camp stove.
Water rushing somewhere below. I lost my footing.

options.label: Put the grate back and mark it

text: Covered. Whatever's down there, stays there.
Too heavy. Left it open.

intro: A storm on the horizon, but it's not rain. The radio's screaming. Hair standing up on my arms.

options.label: Dig in and wait it out

text: Lay flat in a ditch for an hour. Lightning walked right past us.
Waited too long in the open. Something hit near enough to throw me.

options.label: Outrun it to the next ridge

text: Made the ridge. Looking back, the ground where we were is black glass.
It caught us halfway. I don't remember the next part.

intro: A convoy, twenty trucks, parked nose to tail. Doors open. Nobody. Engines still have fuel.

text: Hose, can, patience. Got a good haul.
Fumes. Threw up twice, got nothing.
Glove boxes. Tools, a first-aid tin, a map with circles on it.
Something was living in the last cab. It didn't want me there.

options.label: Leave it. It feels like bait

text: We went around. Later we saw the smoke from a fire where the convoy was.
Leaving it bothered me all night.

intro: Footprints in the dust, fresh. Lots of them, barefoot, going exactly where we're going.

text: A camp. Whoever they are, they left a cache under a stone. We took half.
They knew we were following. They waited for us.
Hours lost. Nothing followed us.
The long way had its own problems.

intro: A hatch in the ground, like ours. Somebody's knocking from inside. Three, then two.

text: An old man and a lot of tins. He gave us some and asked us to tell nobody where he is.
It was a trap, or a madman. Hard to tell which.
We talked for an hour. He sent up a bag on a rope: batteries, and a list of frequencies.
He stopped answering. The knocking went on, though.

intro: Lights out on the plain at night. Moving. Not cars. They stop when we stop.

options.label: Kill the lamp and stay still

text: They went past at dawn. I'm not going to describe them.
I couldn't stay still. They noticed.
They flashed back. Morse. Coordinates. A cache, right where they said.
They came closer. Much closer.

intro: An abandoned workshop on the road. A car on the lift, half fixed. The tools are still on the wall.

text: Took what fits in a bag. The good stuff.
Dropped the engine block on my foot. Mostly my boot.
Slept under a roof for the first time in days. Feel human.
Couldn't sleep. Kept hearing the lift creak.

intro: A mall, flooded to the second floor. The third floor's dry. The escalator's under water.

text: Cold. So cold. But the pharmacy up there is untouched.
Something brushed my leg down there. I came up too fast and hit my head.
Up the drainpipe, in a window. Clothes, tins, batteries.
The drainpipe came off the wall.

intro: A ferry, run aground, tilted. The fuel tanks are on the low side, half under the water.

text: Rigged a pump out of a bike wheel. Filled every can we had.
The hull shifted while I was inside.
Charts, a flare gun, the captain's medical kit.
Just gulls and the smell.

intro: Out on the white, a town. Houses, a church, a water tower. It wasn't there an hour ago.

text: We kept walking. When I looked back it was gone.
I kept looking back. It kept being there.
It's real. A real town, a real well, real people who don't want visitors. They traded.
We walked for hours. It never got closer.

intro: A plane, belly down on the salt. Cargo door open. Crates.

text: Medical supplies. Military. Enough to fill everything we carry.
The crates were nailed. One gave way all at once.
The radio still works. I said our call sign. Somebody, very far away, said it back.
Somebody was already in the cockpit. Still is.

intro: The observatory dome. Inside, a desk with a logbook. The last entry is today's date.

text: Frequencies. Times. A list of names, and ours is on it. Took the book.
The pages are blank except the last one. It says: LEAVE.
A whole room of batteries, still charged. We took what we could carry.
Found it. It was running. Something was feeding it.

intro: The big dish is turning. The control room door is open. A chair is still warm.

text: Pointed it at home. For a second I heard the bunker on it, clear as anything.
Sparks. The whole panel went up. We ran.

options.label: Hide and see who comes back

text: Nobody came back. Nobody at all. We took the spares off the shelf and left.
Somebody came back.

intro: A woman at a stall waves me over. "For you, a special price." She says that to everyone.

text: Talked her down to half. She laughed and threw in a tin.
She talked me up instead. I don't know how.
Heard where a stall keeps its spare batteries. Good to know.
Too many people. Too loud. I left early.

intro: A kid bumps into me in the crowd. Says sorry. Too polite.

text: Got my chips back, and the kid's. Gave the kid's back. Mostly.
Slipped right out of my hand. Gone, with my chips.
Not worth a fight in front of the guards. Felt good, letting it go.
It's eating at me.

intro: On the way out, two men fall in behind me. They stop when I stop.

text: Through a tent, under a tarp, gone.
They cornered me behind the carousel. Took a cut of what I was carrying.
They decided I wasn't worth it.
I was right and they were bigger.
The guards walked me to the road. Didn't even ask for chips.
The guards were on a break. Of course.

intro: An old man repairs radios at a stall in the back. Soldering iron, magnifying glass, a sign: NO PROMISES.

text: He put the iron down. Talked for an hour. About a network, about a night, about what it heard.
He pretended not to hear. Come back another day, maybe.
Two drinks in he was drawing diagrams on a napkin. I kept the napkin.
He drank it and went back to work. Fair enough.

intro: Down in the dam's control room, behind a door marked AUTHORISED ONLY, something is humming.

text: A steel cabinet with ECHO stencilled on it. Still running. There's a logbook.
The door won. My shoulder lost.
Click. Inside: a cabinet marked ECHO, humming, and a logbook nobody finished.
Broke the pick in it. Someone will have to come back.

intro: The observatory's console room. Every screen is dark except one, showing a single point in the sky.

options.label: Read what's taped to the console

text: Numbers. The Voice's numbers. Written as coordinates. And a note.
My hands were shaking too much to read it. We'll come back.
Copied it all, line by line, with the dish turning overhead.
The dish moved. I ran. I'm not ashamed.
